reading.title: Moving to the new Lyon office: what it means for you
paragraphs: Subject: Our move to Confluence in September - what it means for you
Dear colleagues,

As many of you know, our lease on the Part-Dieu building comes to an end next summer. I am pleased to confirm that, after consultation with the works council, we will move to new premises in the Confluence district on Monday 7 September.

The new office has been designed around the way we actually work now. Most teams come in two or three days a week, so the building will operate on a desk-sharing basis, with bookable desks for every team on each floor. There will also be quiet rooms for focused work, a large breakout area and a staff restaurant on the ground floor. Lockers will be available for everyone.

We know that a move raises practical questions, not least about commuting. The site is ten minutes' walk from two tram stops, and we will offer secure bike parking and showers. If your journey becomes significantly longer, please speak to your manager or to HR: we would much rather hear about it now than in October.

Over the coming weeks, your manager will hold a team briefing to walk you through the floor plans, and you can sign up for a guided visit of the building from 15 June. A full set of FAQs is already on the intranet, and we will keep it up to date as questions come in.
Thank you for your patience and good humour while we prepare for the move. I am confident that this will be a better place to work, and I look forward to seeing you there.
Isabelle Ferrand, Site Director

Because most employees now work from home full-time
Because the lease on the current building is ending
Because the Part-Dieu building is being renovated

questions.q: How will desks be organised in the new office?
options: Teams will book shared desks rather than have their own
Every employee will keep a personal desk
Only managers will have a dedicated desk
Desks will be allocated by seniority

options: Wait until October and see how it goes
Ask the works council to intervene
Apply for full-time remote work
Tell their manager or HR now

options: Move their belongings to the new building
Register for a guided visit of the building
Choose their own desk

reading.title: Quality of Working Life Barometer 2026: key findings
paragraphs: 1. Participation

The 2026 barometer ran from 2 to 20 March. In total, 2,140 employees responded, a response rate of 71%, up from 64% last year. Participation remains lower in the warehouses (52%), where fewer employees have regular access to a computer; paper questionnaires and on-site kiosks will be extended next year.
2. Strengths

Relationships within teams continue to be our strongest area: 84% of respondents say they can count on their colleagues, and 79% feel that their manager treats them with respect. Pride in the company's purpose is also high, particularly among employees who have taken part in the volunteering programme.
3. Areas for improvement

Workload is the most significant concern. Only 46% of respondents agree that their workload is manageable, a fall of seven percentage points, with the sharpest drop in Customer Services. Recognition remains below the external benchmark, and the free-text comments point to a feeling that effort is noticed only when something goes wrong. Finally, many employees with caring responsibilities say they do not know what support is available to them.
4. Next steps

Results will be shared with all teams by the end of May. Each director will agree no more than three priorities with their teams and report back on progress in the autumn. Workload in Customer Services will be examined with the works council as part of the negotiations on quality of working life.

glossary.plain: the percentage of people invited to a survey who actually complete it
to be able to rely on someone for help
the unit used for the difference between two percentages
a standard or average used for comparison
the answers respondents write in their own words
looking after a sick, disabled or elderly relative
to tell people what has been done after they gave their views

questions.q: Why is participation lower in the warehouses?
options: Warehouse staff were surveyed later than others
Fewer warehouse employees regularly use a computer
Warehouse managers did not promote the survey
The questionnaire was not translated
questions.explain_fr: « Where fewer employees have regular access to a computer » : d'où l'extension des questionnaires papier et des bornes l'an prochain.

questions.q: What happened to the score on workload?
options: It fell by seven per cent
It rose to 46%
It stayed level except in Customer Services
It fell by seven percentage points
questions.explain_fr: « A fall of seven percentage points » : par exemple de 53 % à 46 %. Une baisse de « seven per cent » serait tout autre chose. Distinction essentielle devant un comité de direction.

questions.q: What do the free-text comments suggest about recognition?
options: People feel their effort is noticed only when there is a problem
People want higher bonuses
Managers thank their teams too often
Recognition is above the external benchmark
questions.explain_fr: « Effort is noticed only when something goes wrong » : on ne remarque le travail qu'en cas d'erreur. Le score est d'ailleurs « below the external benchmark ».

questions.q: What will each director do after the results are shared?
options: Launch a new survey in the autumn
Hand the results to the works council
Agree up to three priorities with their teams and report back later
Review workload in Customer Services
questions.explain_fr: « Agree no more than three priorities with their teams and report back on progress in the autumn » : « no more than » = trois au maximum. La charge de travail du service client sera examinée avec le CSE, pas par chaque directeur.

reading.title: Agreement on Quality of Working Life and Working Conditions (extract)
paragraphs: Article 4 - Right to disconnect
4.1 Employees are under no obligation to read or reply to work-related messages outside their working hours, during rest periods or while on leave. No employee may be penalised for failing to do so.
4.2 Managers shall set an example in this respect. Messages written outside working hours shall, wherever possible, be sent using the delayed-send function.
Article 5 - Working parents and carers

5.1 Employees who are parents of children under the age of three, or who have caring responsibilities for a dependent relative, may request an adjustment of their working hours. Any such request shall be examined in good faith, and any refusal shall be explained in writing.
5.2 The Company shall reserve ten places per year in partner nurseries for the children of employees.
Article 6 - Monitoring and duration

6.1 A monitoring committee, composed of two representatives of each signatory union and three representatives of management, shall meet twice a year to review the implementation of this Agreement on the basis of the indicators listed in Appendix 1.

6.2 This Agreement is concluded for a fixed term of three years. It shall cease to have effect at the end of that period and shall not be tacitly renewed. The parties undertake to open negotiations on its renewal no later than three months before it expires.

glossary.plain: the right not to be contacted about work outside working time
the times when employees are not working, such as nights and weekends
punished or put at a disadvantage
an email setting that sends a message later, at a chosen time
a family member who relies on someone else for care
a group set up to check that an agreement is being applied
a trade union that has signed the agreement

legalese.plain: honestly and with a genuine intention to agree if possible
automatically extended without anyone formally deciding to

questions.q: An employee does not reply to an email sent at 10 p.m. What does the agreement say?
options: She must reply the next morning before 9 a.m.
Her manager may note it in her appraisal
She must reply only if the message is urgent
She cannot be penalised for not replying
questions.explain_fr: « No employee may be penalised for failing to do so » : ne pas répondre hors temps de travail ne peut entraîner aucune sanction. « Under no obligation » = aucune obligation.

questions.q: Who may ask for an adjustment of working hours under Article 5.1?
options: Any employee with more than three years' service
Parents of children under three and employees caring for a dependent relative
Only employees whose children attend a partner nursery
Managers only
questions.explain_fr: L'article vise deux catégories : « parents of children under the age of three » et ceux qui ont « caring responsibilities for a dependent relative ».

questions.q: What must the Company do if it refuses such a request?
options: Give its reasons in writing
Refer the matter to the monitoring committee
Offer a nursery place instead
Nothing in particular
questions.explain_fr: « Any refusal shall be explained in writing » : le refus doit être motivé par écrit. « In good faith » renforce l'obligation d'un examen sérieux.

questions.q: What happens when the three years have passed?
options: The agreement continues automatically for another three years
The agreement continues until a new one is signed
The agreement ends, and negotiations must have begun at least three months earlier
The monitoring committee decides whether to extend it
questions.explain_fr: « Shall not be tacitly renewed » : pas de reconduction tacite. « No later than three months before it expires » : la renégociation doit s'ouvrir au plus tard trois mois avant l'échéance.

reading.title: Sustainability statement: our own workforce (extract from the annual report)
paragraphs: Our approach

Our 6,800 employees are central to our strategy, and our double materiality assessment confirmed that working conditions, health and safety, skills development and equal treatment are material topics for the Group. These topics are overseen by the Executive Committee, and progress is reviewed twice a year by the CSR Committee of the Board.
Policies and actions

In 2026 we renewed our agreement on quality of working life with the unions in France and extended its main principles to our sites in Spain and Poland. Measures include the right to disconnect, support for working parents and carers, and a confidential helpline available in six languages. More than 900 employees took part in skills-based volunteering or used their paid volunteering days during the year.
Metrics and targets

The engagement index stood at 68, two points below our target of 70. The lost-time injury frequency rate fell by 12%. Women accounted for 38% of management positions, against a target of 40% by 2028. Data on employee turnover and training hours are presented in the tables at the end of this section.
Looking ahead

Our priority for 2027 is workload. Survey results show that pressure has increased in our customer-facing teams, and we will report on the measures taken, and their effect, in next year's statement. We recognise that some indicators have not yet been subject to external verification; we intend to obtain limited assurance on all workforce metrics in 2027.

glossary.plain: dealing directly with customers

questions.q: What did the double materiality assessment show?
options: That workforce issues are not significant for the Group
That several workforce topics are significant enough to be reported
That only health and safety needs to be reported
That the Board must approve all HR policies
questions.explain_fr: « Confirmed that working conditions, health and safety, skills development and equal treatment are material topics » : ces sujets sont jugés significatifs et doivent figurer dans le rapport.

questions.q: How did the Group perform on its engagement target?
options: It exceeded the target by two points
It met the target exactly
It has not set a target
It fell two points short of the target
questions.explain_fr: « Stood at 68, two points below our target of 70 » : objectif manqué de deux points. « To stand at » = s'établir à.

questions.q: What does the Group openly admit in the final paragraph?
options: Some figures have not yet been checked by an independent party
The helpline is not available in every country
The agreement was not renewed in Spain
Training hours have fallen
questions.explain_fr: « Some indicators have not yet been subject to external verification » : aveu mesuré, accompagné d'un engagement daté (« limited assurance... in 2027 »). Ton typique d'un rapport crédible.

questions.q: What is the Group's priority for 2027?
options: Increasing the number of volunteering days
Reaching its target for women in management
Reducing workload pressure, especially in customer-facing teams
Extending the agreement to new countries
questions.explain_fr: « Our priority for 2027 is workload », en particulier dans les « customer-facing teams ». Le texte annonce aussi qu'il rendra compte des mesures et de leurs effets.

writing.title: Announcing a reorganisation to staff
writing.brief: You are HR Director at Arvane, a software company. The works council has been consulted on bringing the Sales and Customer Success teams together into three regional units from 1 March, and has given its opinion. Write the all-staff email: what is changing, why, what is not changing, and what happens next.
writing.brief_fr: Vous êtes DRH d'Arvane, éditeur de logiciels. Le CSE a été consulté sur le regroupement des équipes Ventes et Customer Success en trois pôles régionaux à compter du 1er mars, et a rendu son avis. Rédigez l'e-mail à tous les collaborateurs : ce qui change, pourquoi, ce qui ne change pas et la suite.

gaps.text: I am writing to ___ you know about a change to the way our Sales and Customer Success teams are organised.
gaps.explain_fr: « To let someone know » = informer, prévenir. Beaucoup plus naturel que « to inform you of » dans un e-mail interne chaleureux.

gaps.text: The two teams will be brought together into three regional units ___ 1 March.
gaps.explain_fr: « With effect from » est la formule écrite classique pour une date d'entrée en vigueur. « Effective » (sans « from ») est plus américain.

gaps.text: The aim is simple: to give each client a single ___ of contact.
gaps.explain_fr: « A single point of contact » = un interlocuteur unique. Collocation figée, très fréquente en entreprise.

gaps.text: No jobs are affected, and your contract, pay and place of work ___ the same.
gaps.explain_fr: « Remain the same » = restent inchangés. Dites clairement ce qui ne change pas : c'est souvent la première question des salariés.

gaps.text: Your manager will hold a team briefing to ___ you through the new structure.
gaps.explain_fr: « To walk someone through something » = expliquer pas à pas. « To take someone through » est un équivalent un peu plus neutre.

gaps.text: If you have any concerns in the meantime, please do not ___ to get in touch with me.
gaps.explain_fr: « Please do not hesitate to... » reste la formule de clôture standard. « In the meantime » = d'ici là.

writing.model:
Subject: A new organisation for Sales and Customer Success from 1 March

Dear colleagues,

I am writing to let you know about a change to the way our Sales and Customer Success teams are organised.

Following the information and consultation of the works council, which gave its opinion on 14 January, the two teams will be brought together into three regional units - North, South and International - with effect from 1 March.

The aim is simple: to give each client a single point of contact and to reduce the number of hand-offs between teams.

I would also like to be clear about what this does not change. No jobs are affected, and your contract, pay and place of work remain the same.

Over the next two weeks, your manager will hold a team briefing to walk you through the new structure and answer your questions. You will also find a set of FAQs on the intranet.

If you have any concerns in the meantime, please do not hesitate to get in touch with me or with your HR Business Partner.

Best regards,

Hélène Marchetti
HR Director
writing.model_us:

commentary.quote: I am writing to let you know about a change
commentary.note_fr: L'objet est annoncé dès la première ligne, sans préambule. Un e-mail de réorganisation ne doit pas faire attendre l'information.

commentary.quote: Following the information and consultation of the works council
commentary.note_fr: Mentionner le CSE montre que la procédure a été respectée et que la décision est désormais annoncée dans l'ordre : représentants d'abord, salariés ensuite.

commentary.quote: to reduce the number of hand-offs between teams
commentary.note_fr: Une raison concrète, en une ligne. « Hand-offs » = passages de relais entre équipes, source classique de frictions.

commentary.quote: I would also like to be clear about what this does not change.
commentary.note_fr: Phrase charnière qui anticipe l'inquiétude. Dire ce qui ne change pas est aussi important que dire ce qui change.

commentary.quote: your manager will hold a team briefing
commentary.note_fr: On renvoie vers le manager : c'est lui que les équipes questionneront en premier. Le kit managérial doit être prêt avant l'envoi.

checklist: Does the first sentence say what the email is about?
Have I mentioned that the works council was consulted before the announcement?
Have I given one clear reason for the change?
Have I said explicitly what is not changing?
Does the reader know what happens next, when, and whom to contact?
phrasebank: I am writing to let you know about ...
Following the information and consultation of the works council, ...
... with effect from [date].
The aim is simple: to ...
I would also like to be clear about what this does not change.
Your manager will hold a team briefing to walk you through ...
If you have any concerns in the meantime, please do not hesitate to get in touch.

writing.title: Launching a wellbeing programme
writing.brief: Your company is launching 'Feel Good at Work', a wellbeing programme that forms part of its new agreement on quality of working life. Write a short email to all staff presenting the three main services, reassuring people about confidentiality and encouraging them to use the programme.
writing.brief_fr: Votre entreprise lance « Feel Good at Work », un programme bien-être prévu par son nouvel accord QVCT. Rédigez un court e-mail à tous les salariés présentant les trois services principaux, rassurant sur la confidentialité et incitant à y recourir.

gaps.text: In last year's survey, many of you told us that workload and work-life balance were your main ___.
gaps.explain_fr: « Concerns » = inquiétudes, préoccupations. Partir de ce que les salariés ont dit (« you told us ») légitime le programme.

gaps.text: As part of our new agreement on quality of working life, I am pleased to ___ 'Feel Good at Work'.
gaps.explain_fr: « I am pleased to introduce » : formule d'annonce positive et sobre. « To present » serait moins naturel ici.

gaps.text: Our mental health first aiders can listen and point you ___ the right support.
gaps.explain_fr: « To point someone towards » = orienter. « Towards » est britannique, « toward » américain.

gaps.text: These services are entirely ___, and anything you discuss with the helpline remains strictly confidential.
gaps.explain_fr: « Voluntary » = facultatif, fondé sur le volontariat. Préciser ce point rassure ceux qui craignent une démarche imposée.

gaps.text: We know that a programme like this is only ___ of the answer.
gaps.explain_fr: « Only part of the answer » : reconnaître les limites du programme renforce sa crédibilité. Les salariés savent qu'un atelier ne règle pas la charge de travail.

gaps.text: Please take a few minutes to look at the programme page on the intranet, and ___ sign up for a workshop.
gaps.explain_fr: « Do » emphatique devant l'impératif : il rend l'invitation plus chaleureuse et insistante (« n'hésitez pas à »). Très britannique.

writing.model:
Subject: Introducing 'Feel Good at Work'

Dear all,

In last year's survey, many of you told us that workload and work-life balance were your main concerns. As part of our new agreement on quality of working life, I am pleased to introduce 'Feel Good at Work', a programme designed to help you look after your health and wellbeing.

From 1 April, you will have access to three new services:
- a free, confidential helpline, available 24 hours a day, for you and your family;
- workshops on managing workload, sleep and financial wellbeing, held during working hours;
- forty mental health first aiders across our sites. Our mental health first aiders can listen and point you towards the right support.

These services are entirely voluntary, and anything you discuss with the helpline remains strictly confidential. Your manager will not know whether you have used it.

We know that a programme like this is only part of the answer. It does not replace the work we are doing with the unions on workload, and we will report back on that work in June.

Please take a few minutes to look at the programme page on the intranet, and do sign up for a workshop.

With best wishes,

Hélène Marchetti
HR Director

commentary.quote: many of you told us that workload and work-life balance were your main concerns
commentary.note_fr: On ancre le programme dans la parole des salariés : c'est la logique « you said, we did ».

commentary.quote: a programme designed to help you look after your health and wellbeing
commentary.note_fr: « To look after » (UK) / « to take care of » (US) = prendre soin de. « Designed to » présente l'objectif sans exagérer.

commentary.quote: Your manager will not know whether you have used it.
commentary.note_fr: Phrase courte et concrète : elle répond à la vraie crainte des salariés mieux qu'une formule générale sur la confidentialité.

commentary.quote: It does not replace the work we are doing with the unions on workload
commentary.note_fr: Désamorce le reproche de « wellbeing washing » : le programme complète la négociation, il ne s'y substitue pas.

commentary.quote: and do sign up for a workshop
commentary.note_fr: Le « do » emphatique adoucit et renforce l'invitation à la fois. Il disparaît dans la version américaine, plus directe.

checklist: Have I linked the programme to what employees said in the survey?
Are the services listed clearly, with a start date?
Have I reassured readers about confidentiality in concrete terms?
Have I acknowledged the limits of the programme?
Does the email end with a simple call to action?

As part of our new agreement on ..., I am pleased to introduce ...
From [date], you will have access to ...

writing.title: Opening a town hall after disappointing survey results
writing.brief: The Chief Executive, Mark Ellison, will open a town hall the day after the survey results are published. Engagement has fallen by five points and workload is the main complaint. Write the opening passage he will deliver, in spoken style, lasting about two minutes.
writing.brief_fr: Le directeur général, Mark Ellison, ouvrira une réunion plénière le lendemain de la publication des résultats de l'enquête. L'engagement a baissé de cinq points et la charge de travail est la principale critique. Rédigez le passage d'ouverture qu'il prononcera, dans un style oral, pour environ deux minutes.
outline: Welcome people in the room and online
Thank them for taking part and give the response rate
Acknowledge honestly that the results are disappointing and name the main issue
Take responsibility as a leadership team
Say what happens next and when
Open the floor and invite difficult questions
writing.model:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for being here - in the room and online.

First of all, thank you. Seventy-one per cent of you took the time to fill in the survey this year, which is the highest response rate we have ever had. That tells me you still care enough to tell us what's wrong, and I don't take that for granted.

I won't pretend the results are good. Engagement is down five points, and the message on workload is loud and clear: too many of you feel you're running to stand still. Some of that is down to decisions we took as a leadership team, and I take responsibility for them.

So here is what happens next. Over the next six weeks, every team will discuss its own results with its manager and agree two or three priorities. In June, we'll come back to you with a company-wide action plan, and we'll be honest about what we can and can't change this year.

That's enough from me. I'd much rather hear from you, so let's open the floor - and please don't hold back.
writing.model_us:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for being here - in the room and online.

First of all, thank you. Seventy-one percent of you took the time to fill out the survey this year, which is the highest response rate we've ever had. That tells me you still care enough to tell us what's wrong, and I don't take that for granted.

I'm not going to pretend the results are good. Engagement is down five points, and the message on workload is loud and clear: too many of you feel like you're running just to stay in place. Some of that comes from decisions we made as a leadership team, and I take responsibility for them.

So here's what happens next. Over the next six weeks, every team will go over its own results with its manager and agree on two or three priorities. In June, we'll come back to you with a company-wide action plan, and we'll be upfront about what we can and can't change this year.

That's enough from me. I'd much rather hear from you, so let's open it up - and please don't hold back.

commentary.quote: and I don't take that for granted
commentary.note_fr: Transforme un chiffre en message de reconnaissance. « To take something for granted » = considérer comme acquis.

commentary.quote: I won't pretend the results are good.
commentary.note_fr: Phrase courte, à la première personne : l'honnêteté désarme l'auditoire mieux que n'importe quel chiffre positif.

commentary.quote: too many of you feel you're running to stand still
commentary.note_fr: Image idiomatique (courir sans avancer) qui reprend le ressenti des salariés avec leurs mots plutôt qu'en jargon RH.

commentary.quote: I take responsibility for them
commentary.note_fr: Assumer clairement, sans se répandre en excuses : registre attendu d'un dirigeant britannique ou américain.

commentary.quote: we'll be honest about what we can and can't change this year
commentary.note_fr: Gère les attentes dès l'ouverture : on promet de la franchise, pas des miracles.

commentary.quote: and please don't hold back
commentary.note_fr: « To hold back » = se retenir. Invitation explicite aux questions difficiles, qui rend la séance crédible.

checklist: Does the opening sound natural when read aloud, with short sentences and contractions?
Have I thanked people before giving the bad news?
Is the main problem named plainly, without jargon?
Does the leader take responsibility without over-apologising?
Are the next steps dated?
Does the passage end by handing over to the audience?

That tells me you still care enough to ...
I won't pretend ...

I take responsibility for that.

writing.title: A paragraph on our people for the annual report
writing.brief: Write the paragraph on employees for the social section of your group's annual report. Use these figures: 4,250 employees in nine countries; new three-year quality of working life agreement in France; 3,100 hours of volunteering; survey response rate 74%; engagement index up three points to 66; women in senior management 31% (target 35%).
writing.brief_fr: Rédigez le paragraphe consacré aux salariés dans la partie sociale du rapport annuel de votre groupe, à partir des chiffres fournis (effectifs, accord QVCT, bénévolat, enquête, part des femmes dans l'encadrement supérieur).
outline: Headcount and why people matter to the Group
The main measures taken during the year
One indicator that has improved
One indicator below target, stated plainly
The priority for next year and a commitment to report on it
writing.model: At 31 December 2026, the Group employed 4,250 people in nine countries. Their commitment, skills and wellbeing are central to our long-term performance. In 2026, we signed a new three-year agreement on quality of working life with our French unions, covering workload, the right to disconnect and support for working parents and carers, and we have since extended its main principles to our other European sites. Our employees also gave more than 3,100 hours to local charities through our volunteering programme. The response rate to our employee survey rose to 74%, and the engagement index improved by three points to 66. However, the proportion of women in senior management remained at 31%, below our target of 35%. In 2027, our priority will be to reduce workload pressure in our customer-facing teams, and we will report on the measures taken and their impact in next year's report.
writing.model_us: As of December 31, 2026, the Group employed 4,250 people in nine countries. Their commitment, skills and well-being are central to our long-term performance. In 2026, we signed a new three-year agreement on quality of work life with our French unions, covering workload, the right to disconnect and support for working parents and caregivers, and we have since extended its main principles to our other European sites. Our employees also contributed more than 3,100 hours to local nonprofits through our volunteer program. The response rate to our employee survey rose to 74%, and the engagement index improved by three points to 66. However, the share of women in senior management remained at 31%, below our target of 35%. In 2027, our priority will be to reduce workload pressure in our customer-facing teams, and we will report on the actions taken and their impact in next year's report.

commentary.quote: At 31 December 2026, the Group employed 4,250 people
commentary.note_fr: Ouverture factuelle et datée, typique du reporting. Version américaine : « As of December 31, 2026 ».

commentary.quote: Their commitment, skills and wellbeing are central to our long-term performance.
commentary.note_fr: Une seule phrase de principe suffit ; au-delà, le lecteur y voit de la communication.

commentary.quote: and we have since extended its main principles to our other European sites
commentary.note_fr: « Since » + present perfect : l'action prolonge ses effets jusqu'à aujourd'hui.

commentary.quote: However, the proportion of women in senior management remained at 31%, below our target of 35%.
commentary.note_fr: Un rapport crédible mentionne aussi ce qui n'est pas atteint, sans détour ni excuse. « However » marque le contraste en tête de phrase.

commentary.quote: we will report on the measures taken and their impact in next year's report
commentary.note_fr: Engagement de suivi : le lecteur (investisseur, agence de notation) attend une cohérence d'une année sur l'autre.

checklist: Are all figures accurate, dated and consistent with the brief?
Have I avoided vague claims that cannot be measured?
Have I included at least one indicator below target?
Is the tone factual rather than promotional?
Does the paragraph end with a clear commitment for next year?
phrasebank: At [date], the Group employed ... people in ... countries.
... are central to our long-term performance.
In [year], we signed / renewed / extended ...
The engagement index improved by ... points to ...
However, ... remained at ..., below our target of ...
In [year], our priority will be to ...
We will report on the measures taken and their impact in next year's report.

writing.title: An action plan following the wellbeing survey
writing.brief: Following the quality of working life barometer, write a one-page action plan for the executive committee. Include the context, three priorities with actions, owners and deadlines, how progress will be measured, and the decisions you need from the committee (including a budget of 85,000 euros).
writing.brief_fr: À la suite du baromètre QVCT, rédigez un plan d'action d'une page pour le comité de direction : contexte, trois priorités avec actions, responsables et échéances, mesure des progrès, et décisions attendues du comité (dont un budget de 85 000 euros).
outline: Context: response rate, strengths, three issues that stand out
Priority 1: workload, with owner and deadline
Priority 2: recognition, with owner and deadline
Priority 3: support for carers and working parents, with owner and deadline
How progress will be measured and reported back to staff
Decisions required from the committee
writing.model:
Quality of Working Life Barometer 2026 - Proposed action plan

1. Context
The 2026 barometer achieved a response rate of 71%. Team relationships and pride in our purpose remain strong, but three issues stand out: workload, recognition, and support for employees with caring responsibilities. This plan deliberately proposes a limited number of actions, so that we can deliver them and be seen to deliver them.

2. Priorities and actions
Priority 1 - Workload. Review staffing levels and processes in Customer Services, where the workload score fell most sharply, and present the findings to the works council as part of our negotiations on quality of working life. Owner: Operations Director. Deadline: end of September.

Priority 2 - Recognition. Launch a simple peer-to-peer recognition tool and train all people managers to give regular, specific feedback. Owner: HR Director. Deadline: end of October.

Priority 3 - Carers and working parents. Publish a single guide to the support available and help set up a staff network for working carers. Owner: Head of Internal Communication. Deadline: end of June.

3. Measuring progress
We will track the relevant survey items through a short pulse survey in November, alongside sickness absence and voluntary turnover in the teams concerned. Directors will report back to their teams in a 'you said, we did' format before the end of the year.

4. Decisions required
The executive committee is asked to:
- approve the three priorities and their owners;
- approve a budget of 85,000 euros for the recognition tool and manager training;
- agree that each member will sponsor one priority and attend at least one team discussion of the results.

commentary.quote: so that we can deliver them and be seen to deliver them
commentary.note_fr: Argument clé devant un comité de direction : peu d'actions, mais visibles. « To be seen to » = que cela se voie.

commentary.quote: where the workload score fell most sharply
commentary.note_fr: Justifie le choix de la priorité par la donnée, en une subordonnée. « Sharply » = fortement, nettement.

commentary.quote: Owner: Operations Director. Deadline: end of September.
commentary.note_fr: Format télégraphique accepté dans un plan d'action : chaque action a un responsable et une échéance, rien de plus.

commentary.quote: as part of our negotiations on quality of working life
commentary.note_fr: Rappel discret du cadre français : la charge de travail relève aussi de la négociation avec les syndicats.

commentary.quote: The executive committee is asked to:
commentary.note_fr: Formule consacrée pour introduire les décisions attendues. La forme passive évite de donner des ordres à la direction.

commentary.quote: attend at least one team discussion of the results
commentary.note_fr: Demande concrète de « visible leadership » : la présence des dirigeants donne du poids au plan.

checklist: Does the context fit in a few lines and lead naturally to the priorities?
Does every action have an owner and a deadline?
Have I limited the plan to what can realistically be delivered?
Is it clear how progress will be measured and reported back to staff?
Are the decisions required stated explicitly, including the budget?
Does the plan respect the role of the works council?
phrasebank: Three issues stand out: ...
This plan deliberately proposes a limited number of actions.
Owner: ... Deadline: ...
We will track ... through ...
Directors will report back to their teams in a 'you said, we did' format.
The executive committee is asked to:
approve a budget of ... for ...
agree that each member will sponsor one priority.

writing.title: Briefing managers before a difficult announcement
writing.brief: Tomorrow at 10 a.m., the CEO will announce that from 1 March office-based staff will be asked to come in three days a week instead of two. The works council has been consulted. Write the confidential email to people managers, the day before: timing, their role in the cascade, key messages, what to avoid, and the support available to them.
writing.brief_fr: Demain à 10 h, le directeur général annoncera qu'à compter du 1er mars les salariés de bureau devront venir trois jours par semaine au lieu de deux. Le CSE a été consulté. Rédigez l'e-mail confidentiel aux managers, la veille : calendrier, leur rôle dans la redescente d'information, messages clés, ce qu'il faut éviter et le soutien dont ils disposent.
outline: Context, timing and confidentiality until the announcement
The managers' role: explain, listen, leave no question unanswered
What to say: the reasons, what is not changing, individual situations
What to avoid: speculation, improvised answers
Support for managers, including for their own doubts
writing.model:
Subject: CONFIDENTIAL - Your role in tomorrow's announcement on office attendance

Dear all,

As you know from yesterday's leadership call, Mark will announce tomorrow at 10 a.m. that, from 1 March, office-based staff will be asked to come in three days a week rather than two. The works council was consulted on this change and gave its opinion last Thursday. Until the announcement, this information is confidential: please do not discuss it with your teams.

Your role
We know this will be an unpopular decision for some. Your teams will turn to you first, so we are asking each of you to hold a team briefing by Friday at the latest. The aim is not to sell the decision, but to explain it, to listen, and to make sure nobody is left with unanswered questions.

What to say
You will find the full briefing pack attached: a short script, the FAQs and the timetable. In essence:
- why we are making the change: to rebuild the collaboration and learning that newer colleagues tell us they are missing;
- what is not changing: remote work remains part of how we work, and teams will choose their own office days;
- how individual situations will be handled: anyone with particular constraints, such as a long commute or caring responsibilities, can ask for an individual review.

What to avoid
Please stay on message and do not speculate about further changes. If you are asked something you cannot answer, say so, write it down and send it to us: we will update the FAQs every day this week.

Support for you
The HR team will run two drop-in sessions for managers tomorrow, at 2 p.m. and 5 p.m. And if you have doubts of your own about the decision, please raise them with me directly - it is far better to talk them through before you stand in front of your team.

Thank you for your help.

Hélène
writing.model_us:
Subject: CONFIDENTIAL - Your role in tomorrow's announcement on office attendance

Hi all,

As you know from yesterday's leadership call, Mark will announce tomorrow at 10 a.m. that, starting March 1, office-based employees will be asked to come in three days a week instead of two. The works council was consulted on this change and gave its opinion last Thursday. Until the announcement, this information is confidential: please don't discuss it with your teams.

Your role
We know this will be an unpopular decision for some people. Your teams will come to you first, so we're asking each of you to hold a team meeting by Friday at the latest. The goal is not to sell the decision, but to explain it, to listen, and to make sure nobody is left with unanswered questions.

What to say
The full manager toolkit is attached: a short script, the FAQs and the timeline. In a nutshell:
- why we're making the change: to rebuild the collaboration and learning that newer colleagues tell us they're missing;
- what isn't changing: remote work remains part of how we work, and teams will choose their own office days;
- how individual situations will be handled: anyone with specific constraints, such as a long commute or caregiving responsibilities, can ask for a one-on-one review.

What to avoid
Please stay on message and don't speculate about further changes. If you're asked something you can't answer, say so, write it down and send it to us: we'll update the FAQs every day this week.

Support for you
The HR team will hold two drop-in sessions for managers tomorrow, at 2 p.m. and 5 p.m. And if you have doubts of your own about the decision, please raise them with me directly - it's much better to talk them through before you stand in front of your team.

Thanks for your help.

Hélène

commentary.quote: Until the announcement, this information is confidential: please do not discuss it with your teams.
commentary.note_fr: La confidentialité est posée dès le premier paragraphe, avec une consigne explicite. Une fuite la veille ruinerait le séquencement.

commentary.quote: The aim is not to sell the decision, but to explain it, to listen
commentary.note_fr: Structure « not to... but to... » : elle redéfinit le rôle du manager et le libère de l'obligation d'enthousiasme.

commentary.quote: to rebuild the collaboration and learning that newer colleagues tell us they are missing
commentary.note_fr: La raison est formulée du point de vue des salariés, pas de la direction : plus facile à porter pour un manager.

commentary.quote: Please stay on message and do not speculate about further changes.
commentary.note_fr: « To stay on message » = s'en tenir aux messages convenus. Consigne claire, sans infantiliser.

commentary.quote: say so, write it down and send it to us
commentary.note_fr: Trois verbes courts : un mode d'emploi concret pour la question à laquelle on ne sait pas répondre.

commentary.quote: if you have doubts of your own about the decision, please raise them with me directly
commentary.note_fr: Reconnaître que les managers peuvent douter les aide à « own the message » sans se sentir trahis.

checklist: Is the confidentiality instruction clear and placed at the top?
Do managers know exactly what to do and by when?
Are the key messages short enough to be repeated in a team meeting?
Have I told managers what to do when they do not know the answer?
Have I offered support to the managers themselves?
Is the tone respectful of managers' own views?
phrasebank: Until the announcement, this information is confidential.
Your teams will turn to you first.
The aim is not to sell the decision, but to explain it.
You will find the full briefing pack attached.
Please stay on message and do not speculate.
If you are asked something you cannot answer, say so.
The HR team will run drop-in sessions for managers.
If you have doubts of your own, please raise them with me directly.

dialogues.title: Preparing a town hall with the US CEO
dialogues.context: A video call between Greg, the American CEO of the group, and Hélène, HR Director of the French subsidiary. Greg will host a town hall in Lyon next week, shortly after a disappointing employee survey.
dialogues.context_fr: Visioconférence entre Greg, directeur général américain du groupe, et Hélène, DRH de la filiale française. Greg animera une réunion plénière à Lyon la semaine prochaine, peu après une enquête salariés décevante.

lines.speaker: Greg
lines.text: Hélène, hi. So, the town hall's next Thursday. I was thinking I'd open with the growth numbers - get people fired up before we get to the survey.
lines.note_fr: « To get people fired up » = enthousiasmer, galvaniser. « To get to » = en arriver à (un sujet).

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: I can see why, but I'd flip that around. People have just seen their engagement scores drop. If you open with record growth, it might come across as a little tone-deaf.
lines.note_fr: « I can see why, but... » : on valide l'intention avant de proposer autre chose. « To come across as » = donner l'impression d'être.

lines.speaker: Greg
lines.text: Fair point. So what, I lead with the bad news?
lines.note_fr: « To lead with » = commencer par. « Fair point » = c'est juste.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Lead with the thank-you, then the bad news. Seventy-one percent of people responded - that's a lot of people who still care enough to tell you what's wrong.

lines.speaker: Greg
lines.text: Okay, I like that. What are they going to hit me with in the Q&A?
lines.note_fr: « To hit someone with something » (familier) = assaillir de questions ou de critiques.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Workload, almost certainly. And someone will probably ask why we haven't replaced the people who left Customer Service. Expect a few pointed questions.
lines.note_fr: « Pointed questions » = questions incisives, qui visent juste.

lines.speaker: Greg
lines.text: Can we screen the questions beforehand? Back home we usually have people submit them in advance.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: You can collect them in advance, sure, but I wouldn't filter out the awkward ones. If people think the questions are being screened, you'll lose the room in five minutes.
lines.note_fr: « To lose the room » = perdre l'adhésion de l'auditoire. « I wouldn't... » : conseil ferme mais poli.

lines.speaker: Greg
lines.text: Got it. And if I don't know the answer?

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Say so, and commit to getting back to them by a specific date. People will forgive 'I don't know'. They won't forgive spin.
lines.note_fr: « To commit to + -ing » = s'engager à. « Spin » = discours enjolivé, langue de bois.

lines.speaker: Greg
lines.text: One more thing - anything I should steer clear of, legally?
lines.note_fr: « To steer clear of » = éviter soigneusement.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Don't present any change to working hours or the organization as a done deal. Anything like that has to go to the works council first, or we have a real problem on our hands.
lines.note_fr: « A done deal » = une affaire conclue, une décision définitive. Annoncer comme acquise une décision non soumise au CSE expose au délit d'entrave.

lines.speaker: Greg
lines.text: Understood. Can you send me a draft opening by Monday?

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Sure. I'll keep it short - five minutes, tops, and then we open the floor.
lines.note_fr: « Tops » (familier, placé après le chiffre) = au maximum.

questions.q: Why does Hélène advise Greg not to open with the growth figures?
options: Because the figures are confidential
Because the works council has not seen them
Because it could seem insensitive after the drop in engagement
Because the town hall is too short
questions.explain_fr: « It might come across as a little tone-deaf » : commencer par une croissance record juste après une baisse de l'engagement paraîtrait déconnecté.

questions.q: What does Hélène say about collecting questions in advance?
options: It is fine, as long as difficult questions are not filtered out
It is forbidden in France
It is the only way to avoid hostile questions
It should be left to the works council
questions.explain_fr: « You can collect them in advance, sure, but I wouldn't filter out the awkward ones » : recueillir oui, censurer non, sous peine de « lose the room ».

questions.q: Why must Greg avoid presenting changes to working hours as decided?
options: Because the unions would call a strike
Because Hélène has not approved them
Because the CEO has no authority in France
Because the works council must be consulted first
questions.explain_fr: « Anything like that has to go to the works council first » : l'ordre d'annonce compte. Une décision présentée comme « a done deal » avant consultation pose un vrai problème juridique.

dialogues.title: A team leader worried about disengagement
dialogues.context: Tom, who leads a customer support team in the group's Manchester office, has asked Hélène, the Group HR Director, for advice. He is worried that his team is losing motivation.
dialogues.context_fr: Tom, responsable d'une équipe de support client au bureau de Manchester, a demandé conseil à Hélène, DRH groupe. Il s'inquiète de la démotivation de son équipe.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Thanks for making time, Hélène. I'll be honest, I'm a bit worried about my team at the moment.
lines.note_fr: « Thanks for making time » = merci de m'accorder un moment. « A bit worried » : litote britannique, l'inquiétude est sans doute réelle.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Of course. What's been going on?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nothing dramatic. It's more that people have gone quiet. Nobody really speaks up in meetings any more, and a couple of my best people are doing the bare minimum and logging off at five on the dot.
lines.note_fr: « To go quiet » = se refermer. « On the dot » = pile à l'heure. « The bare minimum » = le strict minimum.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Has anything changed recently? Workload, the way the team's organised?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Well, we lost two people in the spring and they haven't been replaced. I suppose everyone's been picking up the slack.
lines.note_fr: « To pick up the slack » = absorber le travail laissé par d'autres.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: That might go some way to explaining it. People often switch off when they feel nobody's noticed how much extra they're carrying.
lines.note_fr: « That might go some way to explaining it » : formule prudente, typiquement britannique, pour « c'est sans doute en partie l'explication ».

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: To be fair, I haven't said much. I've been flat out myself.
lines.note_fr: « To be fair » = pour être honnête. « Flat out » = débordé, à fond.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: That's understandable. But it might be worth acknowledging it openly. A simple 'I know you've been carrying a lot' goes a long way.
lines.note_fr: « It might be worth + -ing » : suggestion douce. « Goes a long way » = a beaucoup d'effet.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And then what? I can't promise them new hires.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: No, and you shouldn't. But you could ask them what would make the biggest difference in the short term. Sometimes it's about priorities rather than headcount.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You mean let them decide what we stop doing?

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Partly, yes. And I'd have a one-to-one with your two quieter colleagues. Not a performance chat - just a proper check-in to see how they're doing.
lines.note_fr: « Not a performance chat » : on précise l'intention pour que l'entretien ne soit pas vécu comme une évaluation.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That makes sense. I've rather been avoiding it, to be honest.
lines.note_fr: « I've rather been avoiding it » : « rather » atténue l'aveu, très britannique.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Quite natural. Let's catch up again in a fortnight and see where things are.
lines.note_fr: « A fortnight » = quinze jours (britannique ; peu employé aux États-Unis).

questions.q: What has Tom noticed in his team?
options: Several people have resigned
People have become quiet and some are doing only the minimum
There are open conflicts in meetings
Absences have increased sharply
questions.explain_fr: « People have gone quiet » et « doing the bare minimum » : signes classiques de désengagement, sans crise ouverte (« Nothing dramatic »).

questions.q: What does Hélène think may partly explain the situation?
options: The team's extra workload has gone unrecognised
The team dislikes the new office
Tom's management style is too strict
Pay is below the market rate
questions.explain_fr: « People often switch off when they feel nobody's noticed how much extra they're carrying » : surcharge non reconnue après deux départs non remplacés.

questions.q: What does Hélène suggest for the two quieter colleagues?
options: A formal performance review
A transfer to another team
A referral to the works council
An informal one-to-one to see how they are
questions.explain_fr: « Not a performance chat - just a proper check-in » : un échange individuel bienveillant, pas une évaluation.

dialogues.title: Briefing a communications agency
dialogues.context: Hélène briefs Jenna, an account director at Northbeam, a US internal communications agency, on the launch of the group's volunteering programme in France and the United States.
dialogues.context_fr: Hélène présente le brief à Jenna, directrice de clientèle chez Northbeam, agence américaine de communication interne, pour le lancement du programme de bénévolat du groupe en France et aux États-Unis.

lines.speaker: Jenna
lines.text: Okay, Hélène, walk me through what you're looking for. Who's the audience?
lines.note_fr: « Walk me through » = expliquez-moi en détail, pas à pas.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: All three thousand employees, in France and in the US. About a third of them work in warehouses and don't have a company email address.
lines.note_fr: Information essentielle pour une agence : elle conditionne le choix des canaux.

lines.speaker: Jenna
lines.text: Good to know. So we can't rely on email. What about screens, posters, team huddles?
lines.note_fr: « Huddle » = point d'équipe rapide, souvent debout.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Exactly. Posters in the break rooms, the digital screens, and a short script team leaders can use in their morning huddles.

lines.speaker: Jenna
lines.text: Got it. And what's the one thing you want people to remember?
lines.note_fr: Question classique d'un brief : le message unique (« the one thing »).

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: That everyone gets two paid volunteer days a year, and it takes two minutes to sign up.

lines.speaker: Jenna
lines.text: Love it - nice and simple. What about tone? Some clients want this kind of thing really polished, others want it to feel scrappy and authentic.
lines.note_fr: « Scrappy » = fait avec les moyens du bord, peu léché (ici positif). « Polished » = soigné, léché.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Authentic, definitely. I'd rather use photos of our own people than stock images. And please, no greenwashing - we're not claiming to save the planet.
lines.note_fr: « Stock images » = photos de banque d'images. « Greenwashing » s'emploie aussi pour toute exagération sur l'engagement RSE.

lines.speaker: Jenna
lines.text: Understood. Do you have a budget for video?

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: A modest one. One or two short testimonials, filmed on a phone if need be.
lines.note_fr: « If need be » = si nécessaire (tournure un peu soutenue, mais naturelle).

lines.speaker: Jenna
lines.text: That works for us. What's the timeline?

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: We'd like to launch in mid-September. One thing to bear in mind: everything for the French sites has to be in French, so please build translation into the schedule.
lines.note_fr: « To bear in mind » = garder à l'esprit. « To build something into the schedule » = prévoir dans le calendrier.

lines.speaker: Jenna
lines.text: Noted. I'll send you a creative brief and a draft timeline by Friday.
lines.note_fr: « Creative brief » = recommandation créative de l'agence, en réponse au brief du client.

questions.q: Why can't the campaign rely on email?
options: Employees ignore internal emails
About a third of employees have no company email address
The agency does not do email campaigns
French law restricts internal emails
questions.explain_fr: « About a third of them work in warehouses and don't have a company email address » : d'où l'affichage, les écrans et les points d'équipe.

questions.q: What kind of tone does Hélène want?
options: Highly polished, with professional models
Humorous and informal
Authentic, with photos of real employees
Formal and institutional
questions.explain_fr: « Authentic, definitely. I'd rather use photos of our own people than stock images ».

questions.q: What does Hélène ask the agency to plan for?
options: Translation of all materials for the French sites
Approval by the works council
A launch in early September
A large video budget
questions.explain_fr: « Everything for the French sites has to be in French, so please build translation into the schedule ».

dialogues.title: Comparing wellbeing programmes with a UK colleague
dialogues.context: Hélène and Fiona, HR Director of the group's UK subsidiary, compare notes on their wellbeing programmes during a call.
dialogues.context_fr: Hélène et Fiona, DRH de la filiale britannique du groupe, comparent leurs programmes bien-être lors d'un appel.

lines.speaker: Fiona
lines.text: So how's the wellbeing agreement going? I gather you had to negotiate the whole thing with the unions.
lines.note_fr: « I gather » = si je comprends bien, d'après ce que j'ai entendu.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: We did. It's part of the periodic negotiations we're required to hold in France, so it's less of a choice than it is for you. But it's been useful - it forced us to look at workload, not just yoga classes.

lines.speaker: Fiona
lines.text: Ha, yes. We've been rather guilty of the yoga-class approach, to be honest. Lots of apps and webinars, and take-up of about eight per cent.
lines.note_fr: « Rather guilty » : autocritique adoucie, très britannique. « Take-up » = taux d'utilisation.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: That's interesting. What do you think the problem is?

lines.speaker: Fiona
lines.text: People see it as a sticking plaster. If you're working sixty hours a week, a meditation app isn't going to touch the sides.
lines.note_fr: « A sticking plaster » (UK) = un pansement, une solution superficielle. « Not going to touch the sides » = n'aura aucun effet.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: Same here. The one thing that's really worked for us is the helpline. Usage is low, but the people who've used it say it made a real difference.

lines.speaker: Fiona
lines.text: We've got our employee assistance programme, which is much the same. Our big success has been mental health first aiders, actually. We've trained about sixty.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: How do you stop it turning into amateur therapy?
lines.note_fr: Question directe mais légitime : elle porte sur les limites du dispositif.

lines.speaker: Fiona
lines.text: Clear boundaries. They listen and they signpost - they're not counsellors. And they get supervision every quarter.
lines.note_fr: « To signpost » = orienter vers la bonne ressource. « Supervision » = accompagnement par un professionnel.

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: That's helpful. We're thinking about doing something similar, though I'd want to involve the works council from the start.

lines.speaker: Fiona
lines.text: Of course. Shall I send you our role description and the training outline?

lines.speaker: Hélène
lines.text: That would be brilliant, thank you. And I'll send you our agreement - the bit on the right to disconnect might interest your board.
lines.note_fr: « The bit on » = la partie sur (oral).

lines.speaker: Fiona
lines.text: Oh, I'm sure it will. Though I suspect they'll find it terribly French.
lines.note_fr: Humour britannique : « terribly French » = très (trop) français, avec une pointe d'ironie affectueuse.

questions.q: Why did the French subsidiary negotiate its wellbeing agreement with the unions?
options: Because the UK parent company required it
Because take-up of its programme was low
Because Fiona recommended it
Because it is part of negotiations required by law in France
questions.explain_fr: « It's part of the periodic negotiations we're required to hold in France » : la QVCT fait partie des négociations obligatoires, d'où « less of a choice ».

questions.q: What does Fiona mean when she calls the programme 'a sticking plaster'?
options: It deals with symptoms rather than causes such as long hours
It is too expensive
It is popular with employees
It was imposed by the board
questions.explain_fr: Un « sticking plaster » soigne la surface : une appli de méditation ne règle pas une semaine de soixante heures.

questions.q: How does Fiona keep mental health first aiders within their role?
options: They only work with managers
They are qualified therapists
Clear boundaries: they listen and signpost, with regular supervision
They report every conversation to HR
questions.explain_fr: « They listen and they signpost - they're not counsellors. And they get supervision every quarter ».

roleplays.title: Presenting survey results to the executive committee
roleplays.situation: You are presenting the results of the quality of working life barometer to the executive committee. Participation is up, but engagement has fallen five points and workload is the main issue. The CEO and the CFO question you.
roleplays.situation_fr: Vous présentez les résultats du baromètre QVCT au comité de direction. La participation progresse, mais l'engagement recule de cinq points et la charge de travail est le principal sujet. Le directeur général et le directeur financier vous interrogent.

turns.say: Right, Hélène, you've got fifteen minutes. Give us the headline first.
turns.model: The headline is mixed. Participation is up to 71%, which tells us people still want to be heard. But engagement is down five points, and workload is the main reason: fewer than half of respondents say theirs is manageable.
turns.tips_fr: Commencez par le message principal, en deux temps : un point positif, puis le problème, chiffré. Un comité de direction anglo-saxon attend la conclusion d'abord.

turns.say: Five points isn't the end of the world. Isn't this just the usual dip after a reorganisation?
turns.model: It may be partly that, but I'd be cautious. The drop is concentrated in Customer Services, where the workload score fell seven percentage points, and the comments are very consistent. If we treat it as a dip and do nothing, I'd expect to see it in turnover next year.
turns.tips_fr: Nuancez sans contredire frontalement : « It may be partly that, but I'd be cautious ». Distinguez bien « percentage points » et « per cent ».

turns.say: What's all this going to cost us?
turns.model: The plan is deliberately modest: around 85,000 euros, mostly for a recognition tool and manager training. The workload review in Customer Services is mainly a question of priorities and staffing, which we'd look at together with Operations.
turns.tips_fr: Donnez le chiffre immédiatement, puis ce qu'il finance. « Deliberately modest » montre que la sobriété est un choix.

turns.say: And what exactly do you need from us today?
turns.model: Three things: approval of the three priorities, the budget, and one sponsor per priority from this committee. If employees see you at the team discussions, the action plan will be taken seriously.
turns.tips_fr: Annoncez le nombre de demandes (« Three things »). Justifiez la demande de parrainage par l'effet sur les salariés (« visible leadership »).

turns.say: Fine. How will we know whether it's working?
turns.model: We'll run a short pulse survey in November on the specific items, and track sickness absence and voluntary turnover in the teams concerned. I'll come back to this committee in December with the figures, whether they're good or not.
turns.tips_fr: Proposez des indicateurs précis et une date de retour. « Whether they're good or not » renforce votre crédibilité.

roleplays.title: Answering hostile questions in a town hall
roleplays.situation: You are on stage with the CEO at a town hall where the move to three office days a week has just been announced. Employees ask you some hostile questions. Answer calmly, acknowledge the frustration and stay on message.
roleplays.situation_fr: Vous êtes sur scène avec le directeur général lors d'une réunion plénière où vient d'être annoncé le passage à trois jours de présence par semaine. Des salariés vous posent des questions hostiles. Répondez calmement, reconnaissez le mécontentement et tenez la ligne.

turns.say: You talk about wellbeing all the time, and now you're making us commute an extra day. Which is it?
turns.model: That's a fair challenge, and I won't pretend there's no tension. We've asked for a third day because newer colleagues told us they're learning too little and feel cut off. But we've built in flexibility: teams choose their days, and anyone with a long commute or caring responsibilities can ask for an individual review.
turns.tips_fr: Reconnaissez d'abord (« That's a fair challenge »), expliquez le pourquoi avec les mots des salariés, puis montrez les garde-fous.

turns.say: Was this decided before the survey even came out? It feels like the consultation was just for show.
turns.model: I understand why it might feel that way. The works council was formally consulted, and its opinion led to two changes: the individual reviews and a review of the whole arrangement after three months. That said, I accept we could have explained the process better.
turns.tips_fr: « I understand why it might feel that way » accueille l'émotion sans valider l'accusation. Donnez une preuve concrète que la consultation a servi.

turns.say: And what happens if we just don't come in?
turns.model: I'd much rather we didn't get to that point. If someone has a genuine difficulty, the first step is a conversation with their manager or with HR, and we'll look at it seriously. What we want to avoid is people quietly ignoring the rule, because that isn't fair on colleagues who do come in.
turns.tips_fr: Ne menacez jamais en public. Ramenez la question vers la solution individuelle et l'équité entre collègues.

turns.say: Will the executive team be in the office three days a week too?
turns.model: Yes. The executive team will follow exactly the same rule, and you'll be able to see that we do. It would be hard to ask it of you otherwise.
turns.tips_fr: Réponse courte et nette : c'est le moment de « walk the talk ». Une longue justification affaiblirait le message.

turns.say: Honestly, how do we know you'll listen this time?
turns.model: You'll know because we'll show you. We'll review the arrangement with the works council after three months, and we'll publish what we've heard and what we've changed. If it isn't working, we'll say so.
turns.tips_fr: Remplacez les promesses par des engagements vérifiables et datés. Les phrases courtes passent mieux dans une salle tendue.

roleplays.title: Convincing a sceptical CFO to fund a wellbeing programme
roleplays.situation: You are asking Richard, the group's British CFO, to approve 180,000 euros for a wellbeing programme in a year of cost-cutting. He is polite but sceptical and wants figures.
roleplays.situation_fr: Vous demandez à Richard, directeur financier britannique du groupe, d'approuver 180 000 euros pour un programme bien-être en pleine année de réduction des coûts. Il est courtois mais sceptique et veut des chiffres.

turns.say: I've read the proposal. A hundred and eighty thousand euros for wellbeing. Frankly, it looks like a nice-to-have in a year when we're cutting costs everywhere.
turns.model: I understand the concern, and I wouldn't be asking if I thought it was a nice-to-have. Our absence rate has risen two years running, and workload is the top complaint in the survey. The programme is aimed at those causes - it's not about fruit bowls.
turns.tips_fr: Accueillez l'objection, puis recentrez sur des faits mesurables (absentéisme, enquête). « Nice-to-have » s'oppose à « must-have ».

turns.say: What's the return? I need numbers, not good intentions.
turns.model: Fair enough. By our own estimate, each resignation in the customer teams costs us around six months' salary once you include recruitment and training. If the programme prevents even ten departures, it more than pays for itself. I'd suggest we agree three indicators upfront - absence, voluntary turnover and the workload score - and review them after a year.
turns.tips_fr: Présentez vos hypothèses comme telles (« By our own estimate »). Proposer vous-même des indicateurs de suivi rassure un directeur financier.

turns.say: And if take-up is low, like most of these schemes?
turns.model: That's a real risk, so we've designed for it. The biggest element isn't an app; it's manager training and a workload review in the two teams under most pressure. And we'll stop anything that isn't being used after six months.
turns.tips_fr: Reconnaissez le risque (« That's a real risk ») puis montrez qu'il est déjà traité. Proposer d'arrêter ce qui ne marche pas renforce votre crédibilité.

turns.say: Could you do it for half the money?
turns.model: We could phase it. I'd fund the workload review and the manager training this year - around 110,000 euros - and release the rest only if the first results are there. That way you're not writing a blank cheque.
turns.tips_fr: Ne cédez pas tout de suite sur le montant : proposez un phasage conditionnel. « A blank cheque » (UK) / « a blank check » (US) = un chèque en blanc.

roleplays.title: Briefing managers on how to cascade a difficult message
roleplays.situation: Tomorrow the CEO will announce that the annual bonus will be much lower this year because of poor results. You are briefing twenty people managers today so that they can talk to their teams straight afterwards. They ask you questions.
roleplays.situation_fr: Demain, le directeur général annoncera que la prime annuelle sera nettement réduite cette année en raison de mauvais résultats. Vous briefez aujourd'hui vingt managers pour qu'ils puissent en parler à leurs équipes juste après. Ils vous posent des questions.

turns.say: Why are we hearing this from you and not from the CEO himself?
turns.model: You'll hear it from him too - he'll announce it to everyone at nine tomorrow. We're briefing you first because your teams will come to you straight afterwards, and we don't want you to be caught off guard.
turns.tips_fr: Expliquez la logique du séquencement. « To be caught off guard » = être pris au dépourvu.

turns.say: What am I supposed to say when people ask whether the directors are taking a cut too?
turns.model: Tell them the truth: the executive committee's bonus has been reduced in the same proportion, and Mark will say so explicitly tomorrow. If you're pushed for details beyond what's in the pack, don't guess - say you'll find out and send us the question.
turns.tips_fr: Donnez une réponse factuelle, puis la conduite à tenir face aux questions hors du kit : ne pas improviser.

turns.say: Honestly, I'm not sure I agree with the decision myself. How am I supposed to present it?
turns.model: That's completely legitimate, and you don't have to pretend to be enthusiastic. What we ask is that you explain the reasons accurately and don't undermine the decision in front of your team. If you have reservations, raise them with me or your director - that's what we're here for.
turns.tips_fr: Légitimez le doute sans renoncer à la consigne. « To undermine » = saper, discréditer.

turns.say: What if someone gets really upset in the meeting?
turns.model: Let them say it - don't try to argue them out of it. Acknowledge that it's disappointing, offer to talk one-to-one afterwards, and mention the confidential helpline if it seems to be about more than the money.
turns.tips_fr: Conseils concrets à l'impératif. « To argue someone out of something » = chercher à convaincre quelqu'un de renoncer à (un sentiment, une idée).

turns.say: And after the team meeting - what then?
turns.model: Send us any questions you couldn't answer by the end of the day; we'll update the FAQ on the intranet every morning this week. And let your HR Business Partner know how your team took it, so we can see where we need to follow up.
turns.tips_fr: Fermez la boucle : questions remontées, FAQ actualisée, retour sur le climat des équipes.

functional.function_fr: Accueillir une critique en public sans se braquer
